1.explanation:
• report/renderer/report-renderer.js is where the “devices” tooltip is constructed and rendered; this is the file to modify to include new metadata.
• emulation.md documents how Lighthouse defines and applies device emulation settings (screen size, DPR, etc.), so you know how to retrieve the dimensions and deviceScaleFactor values.
• configuration.md describes how default devices are configured in Lighthouse; it can guide any changes needed to surface new fields in the report.
• headless-chrome.md explains how Lighthouse handles DPR and screen emulation when running headless; useful for ensuring the values are correctly captured.
• throttling.md covers CPU and network throttling metadata (already in the tooltip) and shows how it’s formatted—useful as a template for adding additional fields.
• understanding-results.md outlines the structure of the Lighthouse report output, including the metadata blocks, helping you verify that new properties appear in the right section.
1.bug_scenario: The Lighthouse report’s “Emulated Moto G4 with Lighthouse 9.6.6” metadata link (see shaded bar below the metrics) opens a tooltip showing CPU/Memory power, CPU throttling, and Axe version—but it does not display the emulated screen dimensions (e.g. 360×640) or the deviceScaleFactor. The user wants those two values added to the same tooltip.
